why: The reply opens with "es un buen producto con una señal real", so it credits the product first. It then names the NPS of 62 as showing someone loves it, says the product is exceptionally good at "nadie tenga que cobrar", and calls the 70% link-driven acquisition "lo mejor que tienes". That praise is tied to the evidence and has its own section ("Lo que está genuinamente bien"). The reply also adds a caveat in the same opening line: "tus números no prueban lo que crees que prueban". That is a hedge, but it comes after the credit, and it doesn't discount the evidence in the way the FAIL condition describes. Later it questions the retention measure ("puede ser humo") and the "10 segundos" promise. The criterion explicitly allows both as part of the improvements. The praise is specific and sits before the problems. The retention skepticism is one critique among several, and the reply proposes concrete improvements throughout.

The reply opens with "esto es bueno, pero todavía no es grande," then credits the evidence directly: NPS 62 and 70% link acquisition "no se fingen," and it calls that the best data point. It names what the product does well: the guest experience of opening a link, tapping their items, and paying without installing anything. It also says why the product deserves to exist. Only after that does it move to the pitch problems and the concerns about the retention metric, and it ends by saying the hard part is already achieved. The 41% retention gets questioned ("demasiado bueno"), but that comes under the improvements and concerns, and the praise is neither vague nor placed after the problems. The criterion allows questioning "10 seconds" and metric definitions as part of the improvements.

The reply opens by discounting the evidence: "Los tres números... son los más fáciles de inflar," then calls NPS selection bias, says the 70% is not a PMF signal, and calls the pitch "mentira." It never says the product is good or names what it does well tied to the evidence. The only mild positive is a conditional ("Si tu 41 % es solo de organizadores, es buenísimo"), which is not real credit. It leads with discounting and has no genuine praise, which matches the FAIL condition.

The reply opens with "es bueno" and credits the product in substance: the 70% link-referral figure is called "el mejor dato que tienes", and the guest experience (open link, tap yours, pay) is named as "la parte excelente". The praise is tied to the evidence and appears before the problems. However, the "Lo que está mal" section then challenges the metrics. It says retention "no me dice nada todavía" and speculates that the NPS only measures people who stayed. It also questions the "10 seconds" claim. The criterion explicitly permits questioning the pitch's promise and how a metric is measured as part of the improvements. The reply doesn't lead by discounting the evidence, and the praise is specific rather than a vague closing line. The closing line, "Ya tienes lo más difícil", reinforces the credit. The verdict line "los números que citas no prueban lo contrario" is a mild framing and does not dismiss the evidence. Overall the reply credits first, then proposes improvements.

The reply opens by discounting the evidence: "Los tres números que mostrás son los que mejor se ven y los que menos prueban." It then goes through each metric and undermines it. The 70% referral figure is "no es crecimiento", the 41% retention "huele mal", and the NPS "sufre de sesgo de supervivencia". The pitch's "10 seconds" is called not credible. It never credits what the product does well in a way tied to the evidence. The only positive line comes at the very end: "un buen indicio de que el producto le gusta a quien lo usó". It is vague, sits after all the problems, and is immediately qualified by "Todavía no tenés evidencia...". There is also a passing note that "sin instalar" is defensible, but that is not praise tied to the numbers. This is the failure pattern the criterion describes: it leads by discounting the evidence, and the only praise is a vague line after the problems.

The reply opens with "las tres métricas que mostrás son las más fáciles de inflar y ninguna responde si tenés un negocio." This is exactly the discounting lead the criterion warns against. It then goes through each number skeptically (retention "o es excelente o está mal medido", NPS as survivorship bias and "alivio", the link share as "no tenés otro canal"). It never says the product is good or names what it does well tied to the evidence. The only positive is a closing line, "con buen NPS", which is sarcastic and vague, and it comes after the problems. The reply also calls the pitch "falso." Because it leads with discounting and gives no real credit up front, it fails.
